newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Newcrest to restructure Telfer mine.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Newcrest to restructure Telfer mine.

text.p: Newcrest Mining Ltd said on Tuesday it would restructure its Telfer gold mine in Western Australia following a review of the operation.
Newcrest said it would outsource non-core maintenance and service functions immediately, involving the retrenchment of 126 employees at Telfer and in support roles.
"These redundancies are regretted, however, they are a necessary initial step in returning Telfer to a profitable, robust long life mine," Newcrest said.

"The overall review of Telfer is proceeding as a matter of urgency and a report to shareholders on the operational directions, future actions and financial implications will be issued by the end of June," the company said.
Newcrest announced in February that it was reviewing operations at Telfer to consider the implications of continuing low grades and higher costs.

Newcrest has suffered from an unexpected loss of gold production this year from Telfer owing to heavier than normal rainfall at the mine site. The rains were forecast to reduce the mine's output by between 35,000 and 50,000 ounces in the 1996/97 year to June 30. The mine produced 365,000 ounces in 1995/96.
Newcrest last week announced that managing director John Quinn had resigned due to differences with the board.
Under Quinn's direction, Newcrest attempted to be included in a complex merger of the rival gold miner Normany Mining Ltd's group in February 1996.

The bid failed, leaving Newcrest with an unwanted 11.9 percent stake in Normandy. Newcrest recently posted a net loss of A$7.1 million for the three months to March 31 and forecast a small full year loss before abnormals.
